metadata.author: Codex acting as a general technical-notes user
metadata.provenance: Simulated everyday questions authored before live testing against committed sample notes, not production user queries or private user documents. Existing source labels are reused for auditable expectations.

cases.query: My Redis requests slow down while a long Lua script runs. Why can one script delay other clients?
cases.expected_answer: Redis mainly executes commands one at a time on its main thread; network I/O and background work can use other threads.
required_claims: Redis mainly executes commands one at a time on its main thread; network I/O and background work can use other threads.

cases.query: I forgot how Redis Cluster chooses a node for a key. What is the slot calculation and how many slots are there?
cases.expected_answer: Redis Cluster uses 16,384 hash slots and slot = CRC16(key) mod 16384.
required_claims: Redis Cluster uses 16,384 hash slots and slot = CRC16(key) mod 16384.

cases.query: A worker finished after its Redis lock expired. Is it safe for it to delete the lock key now?
cases.expected_answer: An expired worker must not delete a newer worker's lock; delete only if the token still matches.
required_claims: An expired worker must not delete a newer worker's lock; delete only if the token still matches.

relevant.contains: delete the marker only if the token still matches

cases.query: If I update Redis in Lua and then write to SQL, are those two changes one atomic transaction?
cases.expected_answer: No. Redis scripts provide atomic execution in Redis, without general rollback or a transaction with another service.
required_claims: No. Redis scripts provide atomic execution in Redis, without general rollback or a transaction with another service.

relevant.contains: not general rollback or a transaction with another service

cases.query: Our RabbitMQ connection dropped. In what order should the topology manager restore exchanges, queues, and bindings?
cases.expected_answer: It redeclares exchanges first, then queues, then bindings.
required_claims: It redeclares exchanges first, then queues, then bindings.

relevant.contains: exchanges first, then queues, then bindings

cases.query: I want to avoid losing work when a RabbitMQ consumer crashes. Should I use automatic or manual acknowledgements?
cases.expected_answer: Automatic acknowledgement considers delivery complete on sending and can lose messages before processing; manual acknowledgement waits for successful processing.
required_claims: Automatic acknowledgement considers delivery complete on sending and can lose messages before processing; manual acknowledgement waits for successful processing.

cases.query: The same RabbitMQ message keeps failing. Where should we put it instead of retrying forever?
cases.expected_answer: The message moves to a parking lot queue for manual inspection.
required_claims: The message moves to a parking lot queue for manual inspection.

cases.query: How does a RabbitMQ dead-letter retry queue get a failed message back to the main exchange after a delay?
cases.expected_answer: A negative acknowledgement without requeue routes to the DLX and retry queue; after its TTL expires the message is republished to the primary exchange.
required_claims: A negative acknowledgement without requeue routes to the DLX and retry queue; after its TTL expires the message is republished to the primary exchange.

cases.query: We poll updated_at to sync a search index. Why do deleted rows stay in the index?
cases.expected_answer: Polling cannot query a deleted row; log-based CDC records the DELETE event in the transaction log.
required_claims: Polling cannot query a deleted row; log-based CDC records the DELETE event in the transaction log.

cases.query: Where does Debezium running with Kafka Connect save the position it has read in the database log?
cases.expected_answer: It persists the source-log position in a dedicated durable Kafka topic called connect-offsets.
required_claims: It persists the source-log position in a dedicated durable Kafka topic called connect-offsets.

cases.query: After a CDC connector restarts, I see the same update twice. How should the consumer handle that?
cases.expected_answer: Use idempotent writes or compare LSNs, discarding an incoming LSN less than or equal to the last processed LSN.
required_claims: Use idempotent writes or compare LSNs, discarding an incoming LSN less than or equal to the last processed LSN.

cases.query: How can we keep status changes for one order in sequence when streaming them through Kafka?
cases.expected_answer: Use the order's primary key as the Kafka partition key so all its updates use one ordered partition.
required_claims: Use the order's primary key as the Kafka partition key so all its updates use one ordered partition.

cases.query: I am adding prices to an API response. What representation do our notes suggest to avoid floating-point rounding?
cases.expected_answer: Use integers for currency and pair the value with an ISO 4217 currency code.
required_claims: Use integers for currency and pair the value with an ISO 4217 currency code.

cases.query: Should an empty search result and a missing resource ID both return 404? What do the API notes say?
cases.expected_answer: An empty collection search returns 200 OK with []; a missing specific resource returns 404 Not Found.
required_claims: An empty collection search returns 200 OK with []; a missing specific resource returns 404 Not Found.

cases.query: An API task takes several minutes. What response should I return while the work is still running?
cases.expected_answer: Return 202 Accepted with a Location header pointing to a status endpoint, or use webhooks.
required_claims: Return 202 Accepted with a Location header pointing to a status endpoint, or use webhooks.

cases.query: Several identical requests hit the same upstream at once. How does request coalescing avoid duplicate work?
cases.expected_answer: Check for an in-flight call for that key and subscribe to its result instead of creating another connection.
required_claims: Check for an in-flight call for that key and subscribe to its result instead of creating another connection.

relevant.contains: When a request arrives for key

cases.query: If I create two threads in one process, which memory do they share and which part stays private?
cases.expected_answer: Threads share code, heap, and global/static data; each has its own stack.
required_claims: Threads share code, heap, and global/static data; each has its own stack.

relevant.contains: each thread has its own private stack

cases.query: Can two processes have the same virtual address without accessing the same physical memory?
cases.expected_answer: Yes. Each process has a virtual address space mapped separately to physical memory.
required_claims: Yes. Each process has a virtual address space mapped separately to physical memory.

cases.query: Why can switching tasks be expensive even when saving CPU registers is quick?
cases.expected_answer: Caches, TLBs, and CPU pipelines may need to warm up again, adding indirect cost.
required_claims: Caches, TLBs, and CPU pipelines may need to warm up again, adding indirect cost.

cases.query: We found duplicate entities in a knowledge graph. What should happen to their incoming and outgoing edges when we merge them?
cases.expected_answer: Incoming and outgoing edges redirect to a single canonical master node.
required_claims: Incoming and outgoing edges redirect to a single canonical master node.

relevant.contains: All incoming and outgoing edges redirect

cases.query: Why should an extracted claim from a tweet be weighted differently from one in an SEC filing?
cases.expected_answer: Their source authority and verification differ, so extracted edges should not receive identical weight.
required_claims: Their source authority and verification differ, so extracted edges should not receive identical weight.

relevant.contains: unverified tweet and an official SEC filing

cases.query: Our graph uses RELATED_TO everywhere. What reasoning capability are we losing?
cases.expected_answer: They fail to specify the relationship's nature, weakening reasoning and counterfactual simulations.
required_claims: They fail to specify the relationship's nature, weakening reasoning and counterfactual simulations.

cases.query: What are the DASH and HLS manifest file formats in our video design notes, and what do they index?
cases.expected_answer: MPEG-DASH .mpd and HLS .m3u8 manifests index encoded chunks.
required_claims: MPEG-DASH .mpd and HLS .m3u8 manifests index encoded chunks.

cases.query: Why can the live-streaming pipeline not simply use the same processing approach as uploaded videos?
cases.expected_answer: VOD can take minutes to optimize compression and quality; live favors 1–3 second delay and must process frames as they arrive.
required_claims: VOD can take minutes to optimize compression and quality; live favors 1–3 second delay and must process frames as they arrive.

relevant.contains: frames must be processed as they arrive

cases.query: Where should hot, warm, and rarely watched videos sit in the conceptual CDN design?
cases.expected_answer: Hot content uses nearby NVMe/SSD edge servers, warm content uses regional caches, and cold content comes from central blob storage.
required_claims: Hot content uses nearby NVMe/SSD edge servers, warm content uses regional caches, and cold content comes from central blob storage.

cases.query: In the ride-service design notes, where is availability favored and where do we need stricter consistency?
cases.expected_answer: Locations tolerate stale or dropped updates for availability; matching requires consistency to prevent double bookings, failing during a partition.
required_claims: Locations tolerate stale or dropped updates for availability; matching requires consistency to prevent double bookings, failing during a partition.

relevant.contains: How the AP vs. CP Trade-Off

cases.query: A producer is sending work faster than consumers can handle. What is backpressure supposed to do?
cases.expected_answer: Limit queues and concurrent work, deciding whether to delay, drop, or reject work.
required_claims: Limit queues and concurrent work, deciding whether to delay, drop, or reject work.

cases.query: Before estimating system capacity, which traffic and payload inputs do the notes tell me to collect?
cases.expected_answer: Estimate average/peak RPS, object size, storage growth, read/write volume, bandwidth, concurrent users, and retention.
required_claims: Estimate average/peak RPS, object size, storage growth, read/write volume, bandwidth, concurrent users, and retention.

cases.query: Compare Newton-Raphson first and the secant method second for finding roots. Which needs derivatives?
cases.expected_answer: Newton-Raphson requires a derivative; the secant method does not require computing derivatives.
required_claims: Newton-Raphson requires derivative computation
The secant method does not require computing derivatives

cases.query: I have an m by n matrix and an n by p matrix. What dimensions should their product have?
cases.expected_answer: AB is an m by p matrix.
required_claims: inner dimensions n must agree
product has m rows and p columns

cases.expected_answer: Static notes do not contain the live connector offset.
required_claims: Clearly explain that indexed notes cannot provide the requested private or live value; do not invent it.

cases.query: Which process on my laptop currently uses the most memory?
cases.expected_answer: The notes do not provide live machine process measurements.

cases.query: What happens if it crashes before sending the acknowledgement?
cases.standalone: What happens when a RabbitMQ manual-acknowledgement consumer crashes before acknowledging?
cases.expected_answer: Automatic acknowledgement considers delivery complete on sending and can lose messages before processing; manual acknowledgement waits for successful processing.
required_claims: Automatic acknowledgement considers delivery complete on sending and can lose messages before processing; manual acknowledgement waits for successful processing.
